questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to avoid being an aggressive driver?

options.text: Not expecting delays on your drive
Keeping a safe distance behind other vehicles
Keeping your hands on the wheel
Not making gestures at other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Not expecting delays on your drive
questions.explanation: To avoid being an aggressive driver, expect delays and plan for them. Keep a safe distance behind other vehicles. Do not make gestures at other drivers. Keep your hands on the wheel.

questions.question: When carrying cargo, you should check it:

options.text: At the end of each day.
Every time you take a break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you take a break.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo and how it is secured every time you take a break. You should inspect it at least every 150 miles.

questions.question: When driving a placarded vehicle toward a railroad crossing, you should always:

options.text: Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.explanation: When driving a placarded vehicle toward a railroad crossing, stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Do not stop, change gears, or change lanes while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Push down on the brake pedal.
Release air from the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push down on the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Using both spring brakes and air pressure together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good idea on long trips.
Takes your attention away from driving.
Is required so cargo stays supervised.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. These activities distract you from the road and are unsafe.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing has no warning gates or lights, you should:

options.text: Not worry because the tracks are likely not used.
Park and walk up to the tracks to check for trains.
Look both ways down the tracks to make sure no trains are coming.
Do what the other vehicles around you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look both ways down the tracks to make sure no trains are coming.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing without gates or lights, look in both directions down the tracks before crossing to make sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: Off-ramps:

options.text: Are usually the safest choice for trucks.
Should not be used by trucks.

questions.explanation: Off-ramps can be dangerous for trucks. Speed limits posted for ramps may be safe for cars but too fast for trucks.

questions.question: If your ABS stops working, how should you brake?

options.text: Press the brake pedal down hard.

questions.explanation: ABS is an extra system that prevents brakes from locking up during hard braking. If ABS fails, your regular braking system still works. You can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: On a leaf spring:
questions.explanation: Check that leaf springs do not have broken or missing leaves. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must be repaired before use.

questions.question: To do a standard parallel parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull directly forward into the space without passing it first.
Back directly into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: For a standard parallel parking maneuver, drive past the space. Then back into it, bringing the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle should fit completely within the space.

questions.question: A 10-foot load must be secured with at least:
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. But all cargo needs at least two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: If you are driving too slowly and may block other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, use your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Check that local laws allow this.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, when air pressure is lost and spring brakes engage:

options.text: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
You can use the spring brakes to drive normally.
The air tanks will refill automatically to a safe level.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
questions.explanation: Dual parking control valves have a separate air tank. If spring brakes engage due to low air pressure, this tank can temporarily release them. Push the correct control to release the spring brakes for a short time so you can move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to get out of your way or warn you. Always signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Help you see a wider area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles have curved convex mirrors. They let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. But they make objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Front wheel braking works:
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works in all road conditions. You are unlikely to experience a front wheel skid, even on ice.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Other vehicles will move out of your way.
You should move slowly and smoothly.
You should wait until you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should move slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This makes your vehicle safer to handle and gives other drivers time to react to your movements.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it is attached to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check each slack adjuster after parking and setting wheel chocks. Pull the slack adjusters to make sure they do not move more than one inch from the push rod. If they move more than one inch, they are out of adjustment and need to be fixed.

questions.question: The most important reason to inspect your vehicle before a trip is:
questions.explanation: The most important reason to inspect your vehicle is to keep yourself and others safe on the road. Safety inspections before every trip are required by state and federal law.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The vehicle is easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose contact with the road and slide on a film of water.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air brakes work:

options.text: Only if you push down the green lever on the control panel.

questions.explanation: Air brakes take a half-second or more to work after you press the brake pedal. Air must flow through the lines first. Hydraulic brakes in cars and light trucks work instantly.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Always watch the road for hazards. Plan ahead for what you would do if a hazard becomes an emergency.

questions.question: In a static leakage test, a triple combination vehicle with air brakes can lose a maximum of ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: The maximum air leakage allowed in one minute for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes is 5 psi. If the leakage is faster, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs to be repaired.

questions.question: When making tight turns, it is important to:

options.text: Open the door for a better view.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. Make extra sure to check them when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight turns.

questions.question: If you must back up, backing toward the driver's side:

options.text: Is only recommended if it is raining.

questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side of the vehicle. This gives you the best view of where you are going.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the safe limit, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: Stop driving as soon as you can. Find out what is wrong. An overheating engine could fail or catch fire.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should:

options.text: Never be done the same way twice in a row.
Always be done in the same order.
Only be done on sunny days.
Not be done if you think the vehicle is fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be done in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way each time. This helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you do not skip anything.

questions.question: Cargo on a flatbed or open trailer must be:

options.text: Loose so it can shift when you turn.
Heavy enough that it will not move.

questions.explanation: Cargo must be securely tied down. This keeps it from shifting or falling off while the vehicle moves.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, check that it is secure every:
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: When avoiding a hazard:

options.text: Swerving may work better than stopping.
You can change lanes without looking.
You should drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may work better than stopping.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. You can usually turn out of the way faster than you can stop. However, swerving can cause a rollover in heavy or top-heavy vehicles or those pulling multiple trailers.

questions.question: What happens if a vehicle runs without engine oil?

options.text: The vehicle will use less gas.
The engine can be destroyed very quickly.
The ABS will not work properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be destroyed very quickly.
questions.explanation: Engine oil is essential for protecting the engine. Without it, an engine can be destroyed in a short time.

questions.question: Where can retreaded tires be used on a school bus?

options.text: On the front wheels of a school bus.
On the rear wheels of a school bus.
They cannot be used on any school bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the rear wheels of a school bus.
questions.explanation: Retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus. They can only be used on the rear wheels.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a problem when checking tires?

options.text: Front tires with at least 4/32 inch of tread
Using radial and bias-ply tires together

questions.correctAnswerText: Front tires with at least 4/32 inch of tread
questions.explanation: Good tire tread is important. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires together, and do not use too much air pressure.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a distracted driver?

options.text: Keep a safe distance from the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance from the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a distracted driver, give them extra space. Stay far enough back to react safely.

questions.question: What is the best practice when backing up?

options.text: Back up quickly to stay out of other drivers' way.

questions.explanation: Backing up a large vehicle is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Use a helper if you can.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a type of retarder?
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow down a vehicle and reduce brake wear. The four types are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.

questions.question: What is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding causes the most deaths and injuries in work zones. Drive carefully and follow speed limits near workers.

questions.question: A 40-foot load needs how many tie-downs?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. A 40-foot load needs at least four tie-downs. Always use at least two tie-downs minimum.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes used?
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are on every wheel of a vehicle. The most common type is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: What does ABS do?

options.text: Stop the air compressor from overheating
Stop front brakes from working on ice
Stop brakes from being used if downshifting is better

questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) prevents wheels from locking up when you brake hard, especially on slippery roads.

questions.question: When checking springs during a vehicle inspection, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that torsion springs are not damaged.

questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, look for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs. Also check for broken or bent coil springs. If your vehicle has torsion bars or other suspension parts, make sure they are not damaged and are fastened securely.

questions.question: What do alcohol evaporators do?

options.text: They add alcohol to air brake systems.
They are only allowed in the northern parts of the state.

questions.correctAnswerText: They add alcohol to air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have alcohol evaporators. They add alcohol to the brake system to help prevent ice from forming.

questions.question: What are air tank drains used for?

options.text: They let rainwater into air tanks.
They remove water and oil from air tanks.
They must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains that remove water and compressor oil. If water and oil build up, they can damage the air brake system.

questions.question: When turning quickly to avoid an object in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Turn more than needed to give extra space.
Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
Steer and accelerate at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
questions.explanation: When turning to avoid an object, turn only as much as necessary. Do not apply the brakes while turning.

questions.question: What must you do within 10 minutes of stopping on the roadside?
questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, you must place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, which action is NOT recommended?

options.text: Try to move your vehicle to the side of the road.

questions.explanation: After an accident, protect the area, notify authorities, care for the injured, collect information, and report the accident. Leaving the scene of an accident can result in losing your license.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report from the previous driver, what should you do?

options.text: Skip your own pre-trip inspection and trust the report.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.

questions.explanation: The first step of a vehicle inspection is to review any inspection report from the previous driver.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, what should the driver do?

options.text: Ignore the report and look for issues themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Skip your pre-trip inspection and rely only on the report.

questions.explanation: For the first step of a vehicle inspection, review the last inspection report if one exists. The company should have fixed any problems listed on the report.

questions.question: What can improperly loaded cargo do?

options.text: Hurt or kill the driver during a sudden stop.
Make it easier to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hurt or kill the driver during a sudden stop.
questions.explanation: Poorly secured or loaded cargo is very dangerous. Loose cargo can fall during a sudden stop and injure or kill the driver.

questions.question: When backing a vehicle with a trailer, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the turn.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
Turn the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: When backing a straight truck, turn the wheel in the direction you want to go. When backing a vehicle with a trailer, turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction. Once the trailer starts turning, turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer.
